fix: destroy tcp/unix sockets after checks

The tcp and socket resource checks called conn.end() on success and on
timeout. end() only half-closes the socket; a still-connecting socket
that times out is left un-destroyed, leaking its TCPSocketWrap handle.
Use conn.destroy() so both checks fully release their connections.

Adds api tests for #82: the server sees the tcp/unix connection closed
after a successful check, and a timed-out tcp attempt leaves no leftover
TCPSocketWrap in process.getActiveResourcesInfo() (asserted directly,
since mocha --exit would otherwise mask the leaked handle).

Addresses jeffbski/wait-on#82

ci: semantic-release with approval gate, commitlint and PR-title lint

Add release automation modeled on semantic-release's own release.yml:

- release.yml (push to master): validate -> dry-run preview -> gated
  release, chained with needs: so a red commit never reaches approval.
  Publish gated by the `release` GitHub Environment; remove its required
  reviewers to go fully automatic (no code change). npm OIDC trusted
  publishing + provenance, no stored token. Version committed back with
  @semantic-release/git. Repo-guarded so forks never publish.
- commitlint.yml (pull_request): lint commit messages against Conventional
  Commits, CI only (no husky). Ignores three in-flight contributor
  subjects so PRs #228/#233/#235 stay green (remove once merged).

- package.json: normalize repository.url to https so provenance matches.
- .npmignore: keep release/lint config and docs out of the npm tarball.
- .github/RELEASING.md: how to approve, go autonomous, set up the trusted

All actions pinned by SHA. Tools run via pinned npx (no new devDeps, no

feat(command): serialize execs and add per-attempt commandTimeout

The rebased command: resource (from upstream #88) ran one exec per poll tick
with no upper bound, so a command slower than the interval stacked up and a hung
command wedged the poll loop forever.

- exhaustMap replaces mergeMap(simultaneous): exactly one exec is in flight per
  command resource, regardless of the simultaneous option, so a slow command is
  never spawned concurrently with itself.
- a new commandTimeout option kills a command still running at the per-attempt
  bound (SIGKILL) so polling continues; default 0 keeps the unbounded behaviour.

test(command): cover concurrency, per-attempt kill, and reverse mode

Replace the rebased command tests (which used jest-style matchers under a
chai/mocha suite) with scenarios matching U11:

- command exits 0 succeeds; a persistently failing command polls to timeout
- a failing command that later passes succeeds
- a slow command never runs concurrently with itself (asserts max in-flight is 1)
- a command exceeding commandTimeout is killed and polling continues
- reverse mode waits until the command starts failing

Real-timer polling with short interval/timeout and node child processes, as the
rest of the suite does; no wall-clock date dependence.

installed @types/wait-on@5.3.4. The bundled types were stricter and broke
existing consumers (jeffbski/wait-on#250):

- the callback typed (err: Error | null) rejected (err?: Error) handlers (TS2345)
- the AxiosProxyConfig / HttpSignature type names were removed (TS2694)
- WaitOnOptions dropped TLS options beyond ca/cert/key/passphrase

Relax the declarations back to the @types shape and add regression tests that
would have caught the break. Verified against the runtime: on success the
callback is invoked with undefined (never null); on failure with an Error.

- index.d.ts: cb (err?: Error); WaitOnOptions extends full SecureContextOptions
  (only ca/cert/key/passphrase are read at runtime); deprecated aliases
  AxiosProxyConfig = WaitOnProxyOptions and HttpSignature.
- test/types.test-d.ts: annotated-callback cases plus a @ts-expect-error proving
  null handling is not forced.
- test/types-compat/dt-wait-on-tests.ts: vendored DefinitelyTyped consumer test,
  compiled by test:types so @types consumers stay unbroken.
- test/api.mocha.js: runtime/type agreement test (err === undefined on success,
  including reverse mode).

feat(cli): add --status-codes flag to accept non-2XX http statuses

`--status-codes CODES` takes a code, an inclusive range, or a
comma-separated list of both (e.g. `200-499`, `404`, `200-299,404`) and
compiles to the existing `validateStatus` option, so a CLI user can wait
on a server whose probe path answers 404 without a .js config file.

It overrides a config-file validateStatus, a repeated flag keeps its
last value, and an empty, bare, malformed, out-of-range (100-599), or
inverted value exits non-zero naming the bad entry.
